ranking.note: Raised to P1: release-binary verification currently passes on revoked/expired keys only — a disclosed security flaw in the tooling operators use to trust binaries, the highest-consequence item on this list.
Raised to P2 and moved up: same class of defect as #36105 (the bitcoin wrapper is simply broken on a supported deployment layout, e.g. Arch), so it cannot sit two bands below it.
Raised to P2: the standalone bitcoin-privbcast tool is motivated by concrete deanonymization/proxy-bypass leaks, a privacy consequence above ordinary new-tool value.
Raised to P2: removes a recurring per-release manual maintenance burden on a user-facing CLI artifact and closes long-standing #17289 after three stalled attempts.
Raised from P4: silently swallowing trailing options such as -rpcwallet is a user-visible misparse affecting bitcoin-cli, bitcoin-wallet and bitcoin-tx, not an incidental cleanup.

Moved up: within this category only the bitcoin-util txoutsetsummary offline-inspection command counts, but that is a concrete new operator capability; the loadtxoutset speedup belongs to another category.
Moved up: a reproducible infinite hang is a real bug fix and outranks groundwork and prototype helpers, even in a niche contrib script.
Moved down: internal dev-script maintainability with a macOS false-pass fix ranks below operator-facing tool bugs and features per this category's ordering.
Moved down: self-described prototype contrib helper for a tracking issue, explicitly optional utility — ranks below bug fixes and tools operators already depend on.
Lowered to P4: clang-tidy refactoring aid with no stated tools-category payoff; the author prefers abandoning it in favour of manual rewrites.

inconsistencies: Chain: #36105 (Windows wrapper exec fix) must be reviewed before #36190, which only adds functional tests for the behaviour #36105 introduces.

#36105 and #36106 both repair the bitcoin wrapper entrypoint (exit-status handling vs. install-path resolution); they are independent but should be reviewed as a pair since they overlap in src/bitcoin.cpp and tool_bitcoin.py.
#35814 supersedes the stalled #18606, #25243 and #30860 and depends on already-merged OpenRPC support (#34683); reviewers should treat the older attempts as obsolete rather than competing.
Chain: #19460 depends on #10102 and #29409 and unblocks #19461; its value is contingent on those landing, which is why it sits mid-band despite being a prerequisite.

#36608 is overwhelmingly a P2P/validation change (121 files); only bitcoin-privbcast falls in this category. Its band here reflects the tool and its privacy motivation and should not be read as the project-wide priority.
#35831 changes ArgsManager itself, which is shared infrastructure; the tools-category benefit (bitcoin-cli/-wallet/-tx argument handling) is what the band reflects.
result.notes: The list separates cleanly: one security defect in release-verification tooling, a cluster of bitcoin-wrapper correctness/deployment bugs plus durable user-facing tooling, then a broad P3 band of developer and contrib utilities. Several cards scored new contrib features (multisig wizard, evalscript) above tool bugs that actually break for users; I reordered so correctness in tools operators depend on comes first, per the category's stated ordering.
